title: Nuh (Noah)
subtitle: The messenger who called for 950 years and built the ship
sources: Qur'an 71 (Surah Nuh, entire)
Qur'an 11:25-49 — the call, the ship, the flood and his son
Qur'an 29:14-15 — a thousand years minus fifty
Qur'an 54:9-15 — the rejected messenger
Qur'an 37:75-82 — peace upon Nuh
Sahih al-Bukhari 4920 — Ibn Abbas on the names of the idols (a saying of a Companion, not of the Prophet ﷺ)

chapters.heading: Nine Hundred and Fifty Years
chapters.body: Nuh عليه السلام was sent to his people with a clear warning: 'worship Allah; you have no deity other than Him' (7:59). He said to them: 'Allah will forgive you of your sins and delay you for a specified term' (71:4). The Qur'an says he 'remained among them a thousand years minus fifty years' (29:14) — that is 950 years. In his own words to his Lord, he called them 'night and day' (71:5); then he 'invited them publicly', then 'announced to them and [also] confided to them secretly' (71:8-9), saying, 'Ask forgiveness of your Lord. Indeed, He is ever a Perpetual Forgiver' (71:10). But every time, 'they put their fingers in their ears, covered themselves with their garments, persisted, and were arrogant with [great] arrogance' (71:7). The leaders said, 'We do not see you but as a man like ourselves' (11:27), and, 'Indeed, we see you in clear error' (7:60). Nuh answered, 'there is not error in me, but I am a messenger from the Lord of the worlds' (7:61). The Qur'an also names the gods his people told each other never to leave: 'Wadd or Suwa' or Yaghuth and Ya'uq and Nasr' (71:23). Ibn Abbas explained that these were the names of righteous men of Nuh's people whom later generations turned into idols (Sahih al-Bukhari 4920). That is a saying of a Companion, not of the Prophet ﷺ.

chapters.heading: The Ship
chapters.body: At last Nuh was told: 'No one will believe from your people except those who have already believed, so do not be distressed by what they have been doing' (11:36). Then came the command: 'construct the ship under Our observation and Our inspiration and do not address Me concerning those who have wronged; indeed, they are [to be] drowned' (11:37). He built it, 'and whenever an assembly of the eminent of his people passed by him, they ridiculed him.' He answered, 'If you ridicule us, then we will ridicule you just as you ridicule' (11:38). When Allah's command came and 'the oven overflowed' (scholars differ on what the oven was; see Go deeper), Nuh was told to load 'of each [creature] two mates' and his family — 'except those about whom the word has preceded' — and 'whoever has believed.' The Qur'an adds: 'none had believed with him, except a few' (11:40). He said, 'Embark therein; in the name of Allah is its course and its anchorage' (11:41). Allah describes the flood this way: 'We opened the gates of the heaven with rain pouring down and caused the earth to burst with springs' (54:11-12), and 'We carried him on a [construction of] planks and nails' (54:13).

chapters.heading: The Prayer of a Father
chapters.body: As the ship sailed 'through waves like mountains', Nuh called to his son, who was apart from them: 'O my son, come aboard with us and be not with the disbelievers' (11:42). His son said, 'I will take refuge on a mountain to protect me from the water.' Nuh answered, 'There is no protector today from the decree of Allah, except for whom He gives mercy.' Then 'the waves came between them, and he was among the drowned' (11:43). Nuh called to his Lord, 'my son is of my family; and indeed, Your promise is true' (11:45). The answer was: 'O Noah, indeed he is not of your family; indeed, he is [one whose] work was other than righteous, so ask Me not for that about which you have no knowledge' (11:46). Nuh did not argue: 'My Lord, I seek refuge in You from asking that of which I have no knowledge' (11:47). In this passage Nuh is told not to ask about what he has no knowledge of, and he at once seeks refuge in Allah from doing so.

chapters.heading: After the Flood
chapters.body: Then 'it was said, O earth, swallow your water, and O sky, withhold [your rain]. And the water subsided, and the matter was accomplished, and the ship came to rest on the [mountain of] Judiyy' (11:44). Nuh was told: 'disembark in security from Us and blessings upon you and upon nations [descending] from those with you' (11:48). Allah says, 'We saved him and the companions of the ship, and We made it a sign for the worlds' (29:15), and, 'We saved him and his family from the great affliction' (37:76). He left Nuh a good name among later generations: 'Peace upon Noah among the worlds' (37:79). Nuh is also remembered as one who prayed for believers: 'My Lord, forgive me and my parents and whoever enters my house a believer and the believing men and believing women' (71:28).

chapters.heading: What to take from it
chapters.label: Reflection
chapters.body: After telling this story the Qur'an says to the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ: 'So be patient; indeed, the [best] outcome is for the righteous' (11:49). Nuh's story is told as a reminder to be patient in calling people to good, even when few listen, and to leave the result to Allah.

familyQuestion: Nuh kept calling for 950 years and very few listened. What is something good you would keep doing even if almost no one noticed — and why would it still matter?

title: Ibrahim (Abraham)
subtitle: The friend of Allah who broke the idols and was saved from the fire
sources: Qur'an 6:74-79 — the star, the moon and the sun
Qur'an 19:41-50 — Ibrahim and his father
Qur'an 21:51-70 — the idols and the fire
Qur'an 37:83-113 — the idols, the fire and the dream
Qur'an 14:35-41 and 2:124-129 — the valley, the House and his prayers
Qur'an 4:125 — Allah took Ibrahim as an intimate friend
Sahih al-Bukhari 3364 — Hajar, Ismail, Zamzam and the building of the Ka'bah
Sahih al-Bukhari 3370 — the blessing on Ibrahim and his family in the Prophet's ﷺ prayer
Sahih Muslim 2369 — 'That is Ibrahim'

chapters.heading: Why Do You Worship Statues?
chapters.body: Ibrahim عليه السلام said to his father Azar, 'Do you take idols as deities? Indeed, I see you and your people to be in manifest error' (6:74). He spoke to his father with great gentleness: 'O my father, why do you worship that which does not hear and does not see and will not benefit you at all?' (19:42). His father answered with a threat: 'If you do not desist, I will surely stone you, so avoid me a prolonged time' (19:46). Ibrahim said, 'Peace will be upon you. I will ask forgiveness for you of my Lord' (19:47), and he left them and what they worshipped. To his people he said, 'What are these statues to which you are devoted?' They replied, 'We found our fathers worshippers of them' (21:52-53). He told them that their Lord is 'the Lord of the heavens and the earth who created them' (21:56). In Surah al-An'am the Qur'an also tells how he looked at a star, the moon and the sun. Each time he said, 'This is my lord,' and each time, when it set, he turned away: 'I like not those that disappear' (6:76). At the end he said, 'I have turned my face toward He who created the heavens and the earth, inclining toward truth, and I am not of those who associate others with Allah' (6:79). Ibn Kathir read this passage as Ibrahim's argument with his people, not a private search (see Go deeper).

chapters.heading: The Idols and the Fire
chapters.body: Ibrahim said, 'by Allah, I will surely plan against your idols after you have turned and gone away' (21:57). When his people had left, he went to their gods and said, 'Do you not eat? What is [wrong] with you that you do not speak?' (37:91-92). 'So he made them into fragments, except a large one among them, that they might return to it [and question]' (21:58). The people asked, 'Who has done this to our gods?' and said, 'We heard a young man mention them who is called Abraham' (21:59-60). When they asked him, he answered, 'Rather, this - the largest of them - did it, so ask them, if they should [be able to] speak' (21:63). They turned to blame themselves, and then said, 'You have already known that these do not speak!' (21:64-65). Ibrahim asked, 'Then do you worship instead of Allah that which does not benefit you at all or harm you?' (21:66). Their answer was force: 'Burn him and support your gods' (21:68). Then Allah said, 'O fire, be coolness and safety upon Abraham' (21:69). 'And they intended for him harm, but We made them the greatest losers' (21:70).

chapters.heading: The Valley and the House
chapters.body: Ibrahim prayed: 'My Lord, make this a secure city' (2:126), and, 'Our Lord, I have settled some of my descendants in an uncultivated valley near Your sacred House, our Lord, that they may establish prayer' (14:37). The Prophet ﷺ told how Ibrahim brought Hajar and her baby Ismail to a place near where the Ka'bah stands, where there was no person and no water, left them a little food and water, and went away. Hajar asked, 'Has Allah ordered you to do so?' He said, 'Yes.' She replied, 'Then He will not neglect us' (Sahih al-Bukhari 3364). The same report tells how Ibrahim later came back and, with Ismail, raised the foundations of the House; as they built, both said, 'Our Lord, accept [this] from us. Indeed You are the Hearing, the Knowing' (2:127). Their prayer continued: 'Our Lord, and make us Muslims [in submission] to You and from our descendants a Muslim nation [in submission] to You' (2:128), and, 'send among them a messenger from themselves' (2:129). The story of Hajar and Zamzam is told in full in the story of Ismail.

chapters.heading: The Dream
chapters.body: Allah tried Ibrahim with commands, and he fulfilled them (2:124). When he went to where his Lord had ordered him, he prayed, 'My Lord, grant me [a child] from among the righteous,' and Allah 'gave him good tidings of a forbearing boy' (37:99-101). When the boy 'reached with him [the age of] exertion', Ibrahim said, 'O my son, indeed I have seen in a dream that I [must] sacrifice you, so see what you think.' The boy said, 'O my father, do as you are commanded. You will find me, if Allah wills, of the steadfast' (37:102). When both had submitted, Allah called, 'O Abraham, you have fulfilled the vision' (37:104-105). 'Indeed, this was the clear trial. And We ransomed him with a great sacrifice' (37:106-107). Allah left Ibrahim a good name among later generations: 'Peace upon Abraham' (37:109). The Qur'an does not name the son in this passage; scholars have named Ismail or Ishaq, and the views are set out under Go deeper. After this passage the Qur'an gives Ibrahim good tidings of Ishaq, 'a prophet from among the righteous' (37:112).

chapters.heading: What to take from it
chapters.label: Reflection
chapters.body: The Qur'an says, 'Allah took Abraham as an intimate friend' (4:125), and tells the believers, 'There has already been for you an excellent pattern in Abraham and those with him' (60:4). The Prophet ﷺ taught his Companions to ask Allah to send blessings on Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, 'as You sent Your Blessings on Abraham and on the family of Abraham' (Sahih al-Bukhari 3370). When a man called the Prophet ﷺ 'the best of creation', he said that this describes Ibrahim (Sahih Muslim 2369).

familyQuestion: Ibrahim spoke gently to his father even when he disagreed with him completely. How can you disagree with someone you love and still keep your manners?

title: Musa (Moses)
subtitle: The one Allah spoke to, who led his people through the sea
sources: Qur'an 28:4-35 — the chest on the river, Madyan and the call at the fire
Qur'an 20:9-48 (Surah Ta-Ha) — the call, his prayer, and the mission to Pharaoh
Qur'an 26:10-68 — the signs before Pharaoh, the magicians and the sea
Qur'an 7:142-145 and 2:51 — the forty nights and the tablets
Qur'an 18:60-82 — Musa and al-Khidr
Sahih al-Bukhari 3411 — Asiya, the wife of Pharaoh
Sahih al-Bukhari 3401 — the long report of Musa and al-Khidr
Sahih al-Bukhari 2004 — the fast of Ashura

chapters.heading: A Chest on the River
chapters.body: The Qur'an says that Pharaoh 'exalted himself in the land' and oppressed the Children of Israel, 'slaughtering their [newborn] sons and keeping their females alive' (28:4). Into that time Musa عليه السلام was born, and Allah inspired his mother: 'Suckle him; but when you fear for him, cast him into the river and do not fear and do not grieve. Indeed, We will return him to you and will make him [one] of the messengers' (28:7). In Surah Ta-Ha the command is: 'Cast him into the chest and cast it into the river' (20:39). 'The family of Pharaoh picked him up' (28:8), and the wife of Pharaoh said, '[He will be] a comfort of the eye for me and for you. Do not kill him' (28:9). The Prophet ﷺ said: 'Many amongst men reached (the level of) perfection but none amongst the women reached this level except Asia, Pharaoh's wife, and Mary, the daughter of `Imran' (Sahih al-Bukhari 3411). Meanwhile, the heart of Musa's mother 'became empty [of all else]', and she told his sister to follow him (28:10-11). Allah had prevented him from taking any wet nurse (28:12). His sister said, 'Shall I direct you to a household that will be responsible for him for you while they are to him [for his upbringing] sincere?' (28:12). 'So We restored him to his mother that she might be content and not grieve and that she would know that the promise of Allah is true' (28:13). Allah reminds Musa: 'I bestowed upon you love from Me that you would be brought up under My eye' (20:39).

chapters.heading: The Man He Struck and the Road to Madyan
chapters.body: When Musa 'attained his full strength and was [mentally] mature', Allah 'bestowed upon him judgement and knowledge' (28:14). One day in the city he found two men fighting, one of his own people and one of his enemies. The man of his people called for help, 'so Moses struck him and [unintentionally] killed him.' Musa said, 'My Lord, indeed I have wronged myself, so forgive me,' and Allah forgave him (28:15-16). Afraid, he was warned by a man who came running that the leaders were planning to kill him, and he left, saying, 'My Lord, save me from the wrongdoing people' (28:20-21). He set out for Madyan, hoping, 'Perhaps my Lord will guide me to the sound way' (28:22). At the well there he watered the flocks of two women, then rested in the shade and prayed, 'My Lord, indeed I am, for whatever good You would send down to me, in need' (28:24). One of the women said of him, 'the best one you can hire is the strong and the trustworthy' (28:26). Their father offered to marry him to one of his daughters if Musa would serve him for eight years, or ten as a favour (28:27). Allah later reminded Musa: 'you remained [some] years among the people of Madyan. Then you came [here] at the decreed time' (20:40).

chapters.heading: The Call at the Fire
chapters.body: When he had completed the term and was travelling with his family, Musa saw a fire in the direction of the mount. He told his family, 'Stay here; indeed, I have perceived a fire' (28:29). When he came to it, 'he was called from the right side of the valley in a blessed spot - from the tree, O Moses, indeed I am Allah, Lord of the worlds' (28:30). In Surah Ta-Ha: 'Indeed, I am your Lord, so remove your sandals. Indeed, you are in the sacred valley of Tuwa. And I have chosen you, so listen to what is revealed [to you]' (20:12-13). Allah told him: 'Indeed, I am Allah. There is no deity except Me, so worship Me and establish prayer for My remembrance' (20:14). He was given two signs, his staff and his hand (28:31-32). Musa feared for his life because he had killed a man among them, and he said that his brother Aaron was 'more fluent than me in tongue' (28:33-34). He prayed: 'My Lord, expand for me my breast [with assurance] and ease for me my task and untie the knot from my tongue that they may understand my speech' (20:25-28), and asked that Aaron be appointed as his minister (20:29-32). Allah said, 'You have been granted your request, O Moses' (20:36). They were told: 'Go, both of you, to Pharaoh. Indeed, he has transgressed. And speak to him with gentle speech that perhaps he may be reminded or fear [Allah]' (20:43-44). When they said they were afraid, Allah answered: 'Fear not. Indeed, I am with you both; I hear and I see' (20:46).

chapters.heading: The Magicians and the Sea
chapters.body: Musa and Harun told Pharaoh, 'Send with us the Children of Israel' (26:17). The magicians threw their ropes and staffs; Musa threw his staff, 'and at once it devoured what they falsified' (26:44-45). 'So the magicians fell down in prostration [to Allah]. They said, We have believed in the Lord of the worlds, the Lord of Moses and Aaron' (26:46-48). Pharaoh threatened to cut off their hands and feet and crucify them, and they answered, 'No harm. Indeed, to our Lord we will return' (26:49-50). Then Allah inspired Musa, 'Travel by night with My servants; indeed, you will be pursued' (26:52). When the two companies saw one another, the companions of Musa said, 'Indeed, we are to be overtaken!' Musa said, 'No! Indeed, with me is my Lord; He will guide me' (26:61-62). Allah told him, 'Strike with your staff the sea,' and it parted, 'and each portion was like a great towering mountain' (26:63). 'And We saved Moses and those with him, all together. Then We drowned the others' (26:65-66). The Qur'an adds: 'Indeed in that is a sign' (26:67). The Prophet ﷺ came to Madinah, saw the Jews fasting on Ashura, and was told, 'This is a good day, the day on which Allah rescued Bani Israel from their enemy. So, Moses fasted this day.' He said he had more right to Musa than they did, fasted it, and told the Muslims to fast it (Sahih al-Bukhari 2004).

chapters.heading: The Mountain, the Tablets and al-Khidr
chapters.body: Allah made an appointment with Musa 'for thirty nights and perfected them by [the addition of] ten', and Musa told Harun, 'Take my place among my people, do right [by them]' (7:142). In his absence the people took the calf for worship (2:51); the full account is in the story of Harun. When Musa came to the appointed place and his Lord spoke to him, he asked to see Him. Allah said, 'You will not see Me, but look at the mountain', and when He appeared to the mountain, 'He rendered it level, and Moses fell unconscious.' When he woke he said, 'Exalted are You! I have repented to You' (7:143). Allah said, 'I have chosen you over the people with My messages and My words', and wrote for him on the tablets 'instruction and explanation for all things' (7:144-145). The Qur'an also tells of a journey to a servant of Allah to whom He had given mercy and knowledge. Musa asked to follow him, and was told, 'Indeed, with me you will never be able to have patience' (18:65-67). Musa could not stay silent about three of the man's acts, and the servant explained each one before they parted (18:78-82). In the long report of Ubayy ibn Ka'b, the Prophet ﷺ said that he wished Musa had been patient, so that more of their story would have been told us, and the servant is named al-Khidr (Sahih al-Bukhari 3401).

chapters.heading: What to take from it
chapters.label: Reflection
chapters.body: Musa's story shows Allah acting through hard things: a baby in the river returned to his mother, a fugitive made a messenger, and a path through the sea. In each case the Qur'an gives the words of trust: 'Fear not. Indeed, I am with you both; I hear and I see' (20:46), and 'No! Indeed, with me is my Lord; He will guide me' (26:62).

familyQuestion: Musa's mother obeyed an impossible command — put her baby in a river — and Allah returned him to her. When has trusting something bigger than your own understanding protected you or someone you love?

title: Yusuf (Joseph)
subtitle: The best of stories — a dream, a well, a prison and a reunion
sources: Qur'an 12 (Surah Yusuf, entire) — 'We relate to you, [O Muhammad], the best of stories' (12:3)
Sahih al-Bukhari 3353 — the most honoured of people with Allah
Sahih al-Bukhari 3372 — the Prophet ﷺ on Yusuf's long stay in prison

chapters.heading: The Dream and the Well
chapters.body: Allah says, 'We relate to you, [O Muhammad], the best of stories' (12:3). Yusuf عليه السلام told his father, 'I have seen [in a dream] eleven stars and the sun and the moon; I saw them prostrating to me' (12:4). His father Ya'qub said, 'O my son, do not relate your vision to your brothers or they will contrive against you a plan' (12:5), and added, 'thus will your Lord choose you and teach you the interpretation of narratives' (12:6). His brothers said, 'Joseph and his brother are more beloved to our father than we, while we are a clan' (12:8). One of them said, 'Do not kill Joseph but throw him into the bottom of the well' (12:10). They asked their father to send Yusuf with them so that he 'may eat well and play' (12:12). When they put him in the well, Allah inspired him: 'You will surely inform them [someday] about this affair of theirs while they do not perceive [your identity]' (12:15). They came to their father at night, weeping, with 'false blood' on his shirt, and Ya'qub said, 'Rather, your souls have enticed you to something, so patience is most fitting' (12:16-18). A company of travellers found him, and he was sold 'for a reduced price - a few dirhams' (12:19-20). The man from Egypt who bought him told his wife, 'Make his residence comfortable. Perhaps he will benefit us, or we will adopt him as a son' (12:21).

chapters.heading: Prison Preferred to Sin
chapters.body: When Yusuf reached maturity, Allah gave him 'judgment and knowledge' (12:22). The wife of the man in whose house he lived tried to seduce him. 'She closed the doors and said, Come, you.' He said, '[I seek] the refuge of Allah. Indeed, he is my master, who has made good my residence' (12:23). The Qur'an says that 'he would have inclined to her had he not seen the proof of his Lord', so that Allah might turn evil and immorality away from him, 'Indeed, he was of Our chosen servants' (12:24). They raced to the door and she tore his shirt from behind; a witness from her family said that if the shirt was torn from the back, she was lying (12:25-27). Her husband saw the shirt torn from behind and said, 'Indeed, it is of the women's plan' (12:28). Later, when the women of the city were invited, Yusuf prayed, 'My Lord, prison is more to my liking than that to which they invite me' (12:33), and 'his Lord responded to him and averted from him their plan' (12:34). He was put in prison. There two young men told him their dreams, and he said, 'I have left the religion of a people who do not believe in Allah' and 'I have followed the religion of my fathers, Abraham, Isaac and Jacob' (12:37-38). He asked them, 'are separate lords better or Allah, the One, the Prevailing?' (12:39). He told one of them to mention him to his master, 'But Satan made him forget the mention [to] his master, and Joseph remained in prison several years' (12:42).

chapters.heading: The King's Dream and the Storehouses
chapters.body: The king said, 'Indeed, I have seen [in a dream] seven fat cows being eaten by seven [that were] lean' (12:43). The man who had been freed remembered Yusuf and went to ask him (12:45-46). Yusuf said, 'You will plant for seven years consecutively; and what you harvest leave in its spike' (12:47), then seven difficult years would consume what was saved (12:48), and after that a year of rain (12:49). The king said, 'Bring him to me.' But Yusuf did not come out first. He said, 'Return to your master and ask him what is the case of the women who cut their hands' (12:50). The wife of al-Aziz said, 'Now the truth has become evident. It was I who sought to seduce him, and indeed, he is of the truthful' (12:51). The king then said, 'Bring him to me; I will appoint him exclusively for myself', and told him, 'Indeed, you are today established [in position] and trusted' (12:54). Yusuf said, 'Appoint me over the storehouses of the land. Indeed, I will be a knowing guardian' (12:55). 'And thus We established Joseph in the land' (12:56).

chapters.heading: The Brothers Return
chapters.body: When the famine came, Yusuf's brothers came to buy food. 'They entered upon him; and he recognized them, but he was to them unknown' (12:58). He asked them to bring their brother from their father (12:59). Later, when they came with their brother, Yusuf took him aside and said, 'Indeed, I am your brother, so do not despair over what they used to do [to me]' (12:69). The measuring bowl was found in his brother's bag, and Allah says: 'Thus did We plan for Joseph' (12:76). When the news reached Ya'qub he turned away and said, 'Oh, my sorrow over Joseph' (12:84), and told his sons, 'go and find out about Joseph and his brother and despair not of relief from Allah' (12:87). When they came before Yusuf again, he said, 'Do you know what you did with Joseph and his brother when you were ignorant?' They said, 'Are you indeed Joseph?' He said, 'I am Joseph, and this is my brother. Allah has certainly favored us' (12:89-90). Then he said, 'No blame will there be upon you today. Allah will forgive you; and He is the most merciful of the merciful' (12:92).

chapters.heading: The Family Together Again
chapters.body: Yusuf gave his brothers his shirt: 'cast it over the face of my father; he will become seeing' (12:93). When the caravan left Egypt, Ya'qub said, 'Indeed, I find the smell of Joseph' (12:94). The bearer of good news cast the shirt over his face, 'and he returned [once again] seeing' (12:96). When they entered upon Yusuf, he took his parents to himself and said, 'Enter Egypt, Allah willing, safe [and secure]' (12:99). 'And he raised his parents upon the throne, and they bowed to him in prostration. And he said, O my father, this is the explanation of my vision of before. My Lord has made it reality' (12:100). His last prayer in the surah is: 'Cause me to die a Muslim and join me with the righteous' (12:101). Allah ends the story by saying, 'There was certainly in their stories a lesson for those of understanding' (12:111).

chapters.heading: What the Prophet ﷺ Said of Yusuf
chapters.body: When the people asked the Prophet ﷺ who is the most honourable in Allah's sight, he first said, 'The most righteous amongst them.' They said, 'We do not ask you about this,' and he said, 'Then Joseph, Allah's Prophet, the son of Allah's Prophet, the son of Allah's Prophet, the son of Allah's Khalil' (Sahih al-Bukhari 3353). In another report he said that if he had stayed in prison as long as Yusuf did, he would have answered the call to come out at once (Sahih al-Bukhari 3372).

familyQuestion: Yusuf said 'No blame will there be upon you today' to the brothers who had hurt him. Is there someone you could begin to forgive — not because they deserve it, but because you deserve peace?

title: Isa (Jesus)
subtitle: The messenger born of a miracle, raised by Allah
sources: Qur'an 3:42-51 — the glad tidings to Maryam
Qur'an 19:16-36 — the birth and the cradle
Qur'an 5:110-118 — Allah's favours, the table, and his words on the Day
Qur'an 4:157-159, 4:171, 3:55, 3:59 — he was not killed, and who he was
Qur'an 61:6 — the good news of Ahmad
Sahih al-Bukhari 2476 and 3443 — his return, and the Prophet's ﷺ closeness to him

chapters.heading: The Word from Allah
chapters.body: The angels said to Maryam: 'O Mary, indeed Allah gives you good tidings of a word from Him, whose name will be the Messiah, Jesus, the son of Mary - distinguished in this world and the Hereafter and among those brought near [to Allah]' (3:45). She asked, 'My Lord, how will I have a child when no man has touched me?' The answer: 'Such is Allah; He creates what He wills. When He decrees a matter, He only says to it, «Be,» and it is' (3:47). When the pains of childbirth drove her to the trunk of a palm tree, she said, 'Oh, I wish I had died before this and was in oblivion, forgotten' (19:23). Then a voice called to her: 'Do not grieve; your Lord has provided beneath you a stream. And shake toward you the trunk of the palm tree; it will drop upon you ripe, fresh dates' (19:24-25). Her people met her with accusation. She pointed to the baby, and they asked how they could speak to a child in the cradle. Then he said: 'Indeed, I am the servant of Allah. He has given me the Scripture and made me a prophet' (19:30). Isa عليه السلام is called a word from Allah, and the Qur'an explains in what sense: 'Indeed, the example of Jesus to Allah is like that of Adam. He created Him from dust; then He said to him, «Be,» and he was' (3:59).

chapters.heading: Signs by Allah's Permission
chapters.body: The Qur'an is consistent: every sign of Isa came by Allah's permission. He told the Children of Israel, 'I design for you from clay [that which is] like the form of a bird, then I breathe into it and it becomes a bird by permission of Allah. And I cure the blind and the leper, and I give life to the dead - by permission of Allah' (3:49). Allah reminds him of these favours: 'when I taught you writing and wisdom and the Torah and the Gospel' (5:110). He came 'confirming what was before me of the Torah and to make lawful for you some of what was forbidden to you' (3:50), and his message was plain: 'Indeed, Allah is my Lord and your Lord, so worship Him. That is the straight path' (3:51). He also gave good news of the one to come after him: 'I am the messenger of Allah to you confirming what came before me of the Torah and bringing good tidings of a messenger to come after me, whose name is Ahmad' (61:6). Yet when he came with clear evidences, some said, 'This is obvious magic' (61:6).

chapters.heading: The Table
chapters.body: Allah mentions that He inspired the disciples, 'Believe in Me and in My messenger Jesus.' They said, 'We have believed, so bear witness that indeed we are Muslims [in submission to Allah]' (5:111). Later they asked for a table of food. Isa prayed: 'O Allah, our Lord, send down to us a table [spread with food] from the heaven to be for us a festival for the first of us and the last of us and a sign from You. And provide for us, and You are the best of providers' (5:114). Allah answered, 'Indeed, I will sent it down to you, but whoever disbelieves afterwards from among you - then indeed will I punish him with a punishment by which I have not punished anyone among the worlds' (5:115). The Qur'an does not say what was on the table, so this story does not guess.

chapters.heading: Not Killed, but Raised
chapters.body: Allah told Isa: 'O Jesus, indeed I will take you and raise you to Myself and purify you from those who disbelieve and make those who follow you [in submission to Allah alone] superior to those who disbelieve until the Day of Resurrection' (3:55). About the claim that he was killed, the Qur'an says: 'they did not kill him, nor did they crucify him; but [another] was made to resemble him to them. And indeed, those who differ over it are in doubt about it. They have no knowledge of it except the following of assumption' (4:157). 'Rather, Allah raised him to Himself. And ever is Allah Exalted in Might and Wise' (4:158). The Qur'an does not give the details of how he was made to resemble another, so no detail is added here. The Prophet ﷺ said, as Abu Hurayrah reported: 'The Hour will not be established until the son of Mary (i.e. Jesus) descends amongst you as a just ruler, he will break the cross, kill the pigs, and abolish the Jizya tax' (Sahih al-Bukhari 2476). The Prophet ﷺ also said: 'Both in this world and in the Hereafter, I am the nearest of all the people to Jesus, the son of Mary. The prophets are paternal brothers; their mothers are different, but their religion is one' (Sahih al-Bukhari 3443).

chapters.heading: What He Will Say on the Day
chapters.body: The Qur'an ends his story with a question on the Day of Judgement: 'O Jesus, Son of Mary, did you say to the people, «Take me and my mother as deities besides Allah?»' He will say, 'Exalted are You! It was not for me to say that to which I have no right' (5:116). 'I said not to them except what You commanded me - to worship Allah, my Lord and your Lord' (5:117). Allah also warns: 'O People of the Scripture, do not commit excess in your religion or say about Allah except the truth. The Messiah, Jesus, the son of Mary, was but a messenger of Allah and His word which He directed to Mary and a soul [created at a command] from Him. So believe in Allah and His messengers' (4:171). So Muslims honour Isa عليه السلام as one of the great messengers, and do not say he is God or the son of God.

familyQuestion: Isa said, 'Allah is my Lord and your Lord, so worship Him.' Why is that one sentence the heart of every prophet's message?

title: Yunus (Jonah)
subtitle: The messenger of the fish who called out from the darkness
sources: Qur'an 21:87-88 — the call from the darknesses
Qur'an 37:139-148 — the ship, the fish and the gourd vine
Qur'an 68:48-50 — patience commanded
Qur'an 10:98 — the people of Yunus believed
Sunan at-Tirmidhi 3505 — the supplication of Dhun-Nun (graded Sahih by al-Albani and Ahmad Shakir)
Sahih al-Bukhari 3416 — 'None should say that I am better than Yunus'

chapters.heading: He Went Off in Anger
chapters.body: Yunus عليه السلام was a messenger: 'And indeed, Jonah was among the messengers' (37:139). The Qur'an calls him 'the man of the fish, when he went off in anger and thought that We would not decree [anything] upon him' (21:87). It says he 'ran away to the laden ship. And he drew lots and was among the losers. Then the fish swallowed him, while he was blameworthy' (37:140-142). The Qur'an gives only these facts, so this story adds nothing about the sea or the fish.

chapters.heading: The Call from the Darknesses
chapters.body: 'And he called out within the darknesses, «There is no deity except You; exalted are You. Indeed, I have been of the wrongdoers»' (21:87). Allah answered: 'So We responded to him and saved him from the distress. And thus do We save the believers' (21:88). The Qur'an also says why he was saved: 'had he not been of those who exalt Allah, He would have remained inside its belly until the Day they are resurrected' (37:143-144). The Prophet ﷺ said that the supplication of Dhun-Nun, when he called out in the belly of the whale, was 'There is none worthy of worship except You, Glory to You, Indeed, I have been of the transgressors'; 'no Muslim man supplicates with it for anything, ever, except Allah responds to him' (Sunan at-Tirmidhi 3505, graded Sahih by al-Albani and Ahmad Shakir).

chapters.heading: The Shore and the People
chapters.body: 'But We threw him onto the open shore while he was ill. And We caused to grow over him a gourd vine. And We sent him to [his people of] a hundred thousand or more. And they believed, so We gave them enjoyment [of life] for a time' (37:145-148). The Qur'an singles this out: 'Then has there not been a [single] city that believed so its faith benefited it except the people of Jonah? When they believed, We removed from them the punishment of disgrace in worldly life and gave them enjoyment for a time' (10:98). Allah then told the final Prophet ﷺ: 'Then be patient for the decision of your Lord, [O Muhammad], and be not like the companion of the fish when he called out while he was distressed' (68:48). Yet He also says: 'his Lord chose him and made him of the righteous' (68:50). The Prophet ﷺ said, as Abu Hurayrah reported: 'None should say that I am better than Yunus bin Matta' (Sahih al-Bukhari 3416).

familyQuestion: Yunus called on Allah from the darkest place. What does it teach you that Allah answered him?

title: Idris (Enoch)
subtitle: A man of truth and a prophet, raised to a high station
sources: Qur'an 19:56-57 — a man of truth and a prophet
Qur'an 21:85-86 — among the patient, admitted into mercy
Sahih al-Bukhari 3207 — the Prophet ﷺ met Idris on the night of the Ascension

chapters.heading: What the Qur'an Says
chapters.body: Idris عليه السلام is named twice in the Qur'an. Allah says: 'And mention in the Book, Idrees. Indeed, he was a man of truth and a prophet. And We raised him to a high station' (19:56-57). The Qur'an says no more about his life, and this story does not fill the silence.

chapters.heading: Among the Patient
chapters.body: 'And [mention] Ishmael and Idrees and Dhul-Kifl; all were of the patient. And We admitted them into Our mercy. Indeed, they were of the righteous' (21:85-86). On the night of the Ascension the Prophet ﷺ met him in the heavens. In the report of Malik bin Sasaa he said that in the fourth heaven: 'There I met Idris and greeted him. He said, «You are welcomed O brother and Prophet»' (Sahih al-Bukhari 3207). Some reports place him in a different heaven, so the heaven is not a point to rely on. What the Qur'an and the Prophet ﷺ confirm is that he was truthful, patient and honoured.

familyQuestion: Allah calls Idris a man of truth. What makes someone truthful in small things, not only big ones?

title: Hud
subtitle: The prophet sent to 'Ad, the people of the lofty pillars
sources: Qur'an 7:65-72 — the warning to 'Ad
Qur'an 11:50-60 — his words and their end
Qur'an 26:123-140 — what he said of their buildings
Qur'an 46:21-26 and 69:6-8 — the wind
Qur'an 89:6-8 and 41:15 — Iram and their boast of strength

chapters.heading: The People of the Pillars
chapters.body: Allah says: 'And to the «Aad [We sent] their brother Hud. He said, «O my people, worship Allah; you have no deity other than Him. Then will you not fear Him?»' (7:65). He reminded them that Allah 'made you successors after the people of Noah and increased you in stature extensively' (7:69). The Qur'an describes their buildings: 'Iram - who had lofty pillars, The likes of whom had never been created in the land' (89:7-8). Hud عليه السلام said to them: 'Do you construct on every elevation a sign, amusing yourselves, And take for yourselves palaces and fortresses that you might abide eternally? And when you strike, you strike as tyrants' (26:128-130). Their boast was: 'Who is greater than us in strength?' (41:15).

chapters.heading: What They Answered
chapters.body: Hud asked for no payment: 'My reward is only from the one who created me. Then will you not reason?' (11:51). He told them, 'ask forgiveness of your Lord and then repent to Him. He will send [rain from] the sky upon you in showers and increase you in strength [added] to your strength' (11:52). The eminent ones said, 'Indeed, we see you in foolishness, and indeed, we think you are of the liars' (7:66). He answered, 'there is not foolishness in me, but I am a messenger from the Lord of the worlds' (7:67). They said, 'we are not ones to leave our gods on your say-so' (11:53). Hud replied, 'Indeed, I have relied upon Allah, my Lord and your Lord' (11:56).

chapters.heading: The Wind
chapters.body: When they saw a cloud approaching their valleys they said, 'This is a cloud bringing us rain!' Allah said: 'Rather, it is that for which you were impatient: a wind, within it a painful punishment, Destroying everything by command of its Lord' (46:24-25). It was 'a screaming, violent wind Which Allah imposed upon them for seven nights and eight days in succession, so you would see the people therein fallen as if they were hollow trunks of palm trees' (69:6-7). 'Then do you see of them any remains?' (69:8). 'And when Our command came, We saved Hud and those who believed with him, by mercy from Us' (11:58).

familyQuestion: 'Ad trusted in their strength and buildings. What do you rely on, and what did Hud rely on?

title: Salih
subtitle: The prophet sent to Thamud with the she-camel of Allah
sources: Qur'an 7:73-79 — the she-camel of Allah
Qur'an 11:61-68 — the shriek that seized them
Qur'an 26:141-159 — his words and the shared drink
Qur'an 54:23-31 and 91:11-15 — the most wretched of them
Sahih al-Bukhari 3380 — the Prophet ﷺ at Al-Hijr

chapters.heading: A Sign from Allah
chapters.body: Allah says: 'And to the Thamud [We sent] their brother Salih. He said, «O my people, worship Allah; you have no deity other than Him. There has come to you clear evidence from your Lord. This is the she-camel of Allah [sent] to you as a sign. So leave her to eat within Allah's land and do not touch her with harm, lest there seize you a painful punishment»' (7:73). Salih عليه السلام reminded them of their blessings: 'you take for yourselves palaces from its plains and carve from the mountains, homes. Then remember the favors of Allah and do not commit abuse on the earth, spreading corruption' (7:74). He said of the she-camel, 'For her is a [time of] drink, and for you is a [time of] drink, [each] on a known day. And do not touch her with harm, lest you be seized by the punishment of a terrible day' (26:155-156). He asked for no payment: 'My payment is only from the Lord of the worlds' (26:145).

chapters.heading: The Arrogant and the Believers
chapters.body: The Qur'an records a conversation between two groups. 'Said the eminent ones who were arrogant among his people to those who were oppressed - to those who believed among them, «Do you [actually] know that Salih is sent from his Lord?» They said, «Indeed we, in that with which he was sent, are believers.» Said those who were arrogant, «Indeed we, in that which you have believed, are disbelievers»' (7:75-76). Others said, 'Is it one human being among us that we should follow?' (54:24). Salih answered, 'O my people, have you considered: if I should be upon clear evidence from my Lord and He has given me mercy from Himself, who would protect me from Allah if I disobeyed Him?' (11:63).

chapters.heading: The Shriek
chapters.body: 'The most wretched of them was sent forth' (91:12). 'So they hamstrung the she-camel and were insolent toward the command of their Lord and said, «O Salih, bring us what you promise us, if you should be of the messengers»' (7:77). Salih said, 'Enjoy yourselves in your homes for three days. That is a promise not to be denied' (11:65). Then: 'We saved Salih and those who believed with him, by mercy from Us' (11:66), 'And the shriek seized those who had wronged, and they became within their homes [corpses] fallen prone' (11:67). Salih 'turned away from them and said, «O my people, I had certainly conveyed to you the message of my Lord and advised you, but you do not like advisors»' (7:79). When the Prophet ﷺ passed by Al-Hijr, where Thamud had lived, he said, according to Ibn Umar: 'Do not enter the houses of those who were unjust to themselves, unless (you enter) weeping, lest you should suffer the same punishment as was inflicted upon them' (Sahih al-Bukhari 3380).

familyQuestion: The she-camel came with a rule: a shared day for her drink. What gifts has Allah given you that come with a duty to share?

title: Lut (Lot)
subtitle: The messenger who warned a people who went beyond all limits
sources: Qur'an 7:80-84 — the warning and the answer
Qur'an 11:77-83 and 15:57-77 — the angels, the night and the morning
Qur'an 26:160-175 and 29:28-35 — his words and his supplication
Qur'an 51:31-37 and 66:10 — one house of Muslims, and his wife
Sahih al-Bukhari 3372 — the Prophet ﷺ on Lut

chapters.heading: The Warning
chapters.body: Lut عليه السلام said to his people: 'Do you commit such immorality as no one has preceded you with from among the worlds? Indeed, you approach men with desire, instead of women. Rather, you are a transgressing people' (7:80-81). He said: 'Will you not fear Allah? Indeed, I am to you a trustworthy messenger. So fear Allah and obey me. And I do not ask you for it any payment' (26:161-164). The Qur'an adds that they also 'obstruct the road and commit in your meetings [every] evil' (29:29). His people answered: 'Evict them from your city! Indeed, they are men who keep themselves pure' (7:82), and 'If you do not desist, O Lot, you will surely be of those evicted' (26:167). He said, 'Indeed, I am, toward your deed, of those who detest [it]. My Lord, save me and my family from [the consequence of] what they do' (26:168-169).

chapters.heading: The Angels
chapters.body: The angels first came to Ibrahim, and told him: 'We have been sent to the people of Lot' (11:70). Then they came to Lut: 'he was anguished for them and felt for them great discomfort and said, «This is a trying day»' (11:77). His people came hastening to him. He said, 'fear Allah and do not disgrace me concerning my guests' (11:78) and 'If only I had against you some power or could take refuge in a strong support' (11:80). The Prophet ﷺ said: 'may Allah send His Mercy on Lot! He wished to have a powerful support' (Sahih al-Bukhari 3372). The angels said: 'O Lot, indeed we are messengers of your Lord; [therefore], they will never reach you. So set out with your family during a portion of the night and let not any among you look back - except your wife; indeed, she will be struck by that which strikes them. Indeed, their appointment is [for] the morning. Is not the morning near?' (11:81).

chapters.heading: The Morning
chapters.body: 'So the shriek seized them at sunrise. And We made the highest part [of the city] its lowest and rained upon them stones of hard clay. Indeed in that are signs for those who discern' (15:73-75). Allah says of those cities that they are 'on an established road' (15:76), and 'Indeed in that is a sign for the believers' (15:77). The Qur'an says: 'So We brought out whoever was in the cities of the believers. And We found not within them other than a [single] house of Muslims' (51:35-36). Lut's wife was not saved: 'We saved him and his family, except for his wife; she was of those who remained [with the evildoers]' (7:83). Allah gives her as a lesson: she and the wife of Noah 'were under two of Our righteous servants but betrayed them, so those prophets did not avail them from Allah at all' (66:10). Allah also counts him among the chosen: 'Ishmael and Elisha and Jonah and Lot - and all [of them] We preferred over the worlds' (6:86).

familyQuestion: Lut kept calling his people to Allah even though almost none listened. Where do you find the strength to keep doing right when you stand almost alone?

title: Ismail (Ishmael)
subtitle: True to his promise, who raised the House with his father
sources: Qur'an 14:35-41 — Ibrahim's prayer for the valley
Qur'an 19:54-55 — true to his promise, a messenger and prophet
Qur'an 2:125-129 — raising the foundations of the House
Qur'an 37:100-113 — the forbearing boy (his name is not stated in these verses)
Sahih al-Bukhari 3364 — Hajar, Ismail, Zamzam and the building of the Ka'bah

chapters.heading: The Valley
chapters.body: Ibrahim عليه السلام prayed: 'Our Lord, I have settled some of my descendants in an uncultivated valley near Your sacred House, our Lord, that they may establish prayer. So make hearts among the people incline toward them and provide for them from the fruits that they might be grateful' (14:37). Ibn Abbas reported the Prophet's ﷺ account (Sahih al-Bukhari 3364). Ibrahim brought Hajar and her son Ismail 'to a place near the Ka'ba under a tree on the spot of Zamzam' where 'there was nobody in Mecca, nor was there any water.' He left them with dates and a water-skin. Hajar asked, 'Has Allah ordered you to do so?' He said, 'Yes.' She said, 'Then He will not neglect us.' When the water was used up, she went between the mountains of Safa and Marwa, seven times. The Prophet ﷺ said, 'This is the source of the tradition of the walking of people between them.' Then she heard a voice and saw an angel at the place of Zamzam, digging the earth, till water flowed.

chapters.heading: Growing Up in Makkah
chapters.body: The same report says the Prophet ﷺ added, 'May Allah bestow Mercy on Ishmael's mother! Had she let the Zamzam (flow without trying to control it) (or had she not scooped from that water) (to fill her water-skin), Zamzam would have been a stream flowing on the surface of the earth.' The angel told her: 'Don't be afraid of being neglected, for this is the House of Allah which will be built by this boy and his father, and Allah never neglects His people.' Later the tribe of Jurhum came to the valley, saw a bird circling over water and settled there with her permission. Ismail grew up among them and learned Arabic from them (Sahih al-Bukhari 3364).

chapters.heading: A Messenger True to His Promise
chapters.body: Allah says: 'And mention in the Book, Ishmael. Indeed, he was true to his promise, and he was a messenger and a prophet. And he used to enjoin on his people prayer and zakah and was to his Lord pleasing' (19:54-55). Allah counts him among the outstanding: 'And remember Ishmael, Elisha and Dhul-Kifl, and all are among the outstanding' (38:48), and among the patient (21:85). Allah also says, 'And Ishmael and Elisha and Jonah and Lot - and all [of them] We preferred over the worlds' (6:86). In the verses on the sacrifice, the Qur'an calls the boy 'a forbearing boy' who said, 'O my father, do as you are commanded. You will find me, if Allah wills, of the steadfast' (37:101-102). The Qur'an does not name him in these verses, and scholars differ over which son it was. This story does not choose between them.

chapters.heading: Raising the House
chapters.body: Ibrahim told Ismail, 'Allah has ordered me to build a house here.' Ismail said, 'I will help you.' Ismail brought the stones and Ibrahim built (Sahih al-Bukhari 3364). The Qur'an says: 'And [mention] when Abraham was raising the foundations of the House and [with him] Ishmael, [saying], «Our Lord, accept [this] from us. Indeed You are the Hearing, the Knowing. Our Lord, and make us Muslims [in submission] to You and from our descendants a Muslim nation [in submission] to You»' (2:127-128). They prayed for a messenger among them: 'send among them a messenger from themselves who will recite to them Your verses and teach them the Book and wisdom and purify them' (2:129). Allah charged them: 'Purify My House for those who perform Tawaf and those who are staying [there] for worship and those who bow and prostrate [in prayer]' (2:125).

familyQuestion: Hajar said, 'Then He will not neglect us.' When have you needed that kind of trust in Allah?

title: Dawud (David)
subtitle: The king and prophet who was given the Zabur and often turned back to Allah
sources: Qur'an 2:246-251 — Saul, Goliath and the kingship given to Dawud
Qur'an 38:17-26 — the possessor of strength, the two adversaries
Qur'an 34:10-13 and 21:78-80 — the mountains, the birds and the iron
Qur'an 17:55 and 4:163 — the Zabur (Psalms)
Sahih al-Bukhari 3417, 2073 and 3420 — the Prophet's ﷺ words on Dawud

chapters.heading: The Giant and the Kingdom
chapters.body: The Qur'an tells that the Children of Israel were told: 'Indeed, Allah has sent to you Saul as a king' (2:247). When Saul's army faced Goliath, they said: 'Our Lord, pour upon us patience and plant firmly our feet and give us victory over the disbelieving people' (2:250). Then: 'So they defeated them by permission of Allah, and David killed Goliath, and Allah gave him the kingship and prophethood and taught him from that which He willed' (2:251). The Qur'an does not give the details of the fight, so this story does not add them.

chapters.heading: Strength and Repentance
chapters.body: Allah told the final Prophet ﷺ: 'remember Our servant, David, the possessor of strength; indeed, he was one who repeatedly turned back [to Allah]' (38:17). 'Indeed, We subjected the mountains [to praise] with him, exalting [Allah] in the [late] afternoon and [after] sunrise. And the birds were assembled, all with him repeating [praises]' (38:18-19). 'And We strengthened his kingdom and gave him wisdom and discernment in speech' (38:20). Allah 'made pliable for him iron', and said: 'Make full coats of mail and calculate [precisely] the links, and work [all of you] righteousness' (34:10-11). To David Allah gave 'the book [of Psalms]' (17:55).

chapters.heading: The Two Adversaries
chapters.body: The Qur'an tells of two men who climbed over the wall of his prayer chamber and said: 'Indeed this, my brother, has ninety-nine ewes, and I have one ewe; so he said, «Entrust her to me,» and he overpowered me in speech' (38:23). David judged, then: 'David became certain that We had tried him, and he asked forgiveness of his Lord and fell down bowing [in prostration] and turned in repentance [to Allah]' (38:24). Allah said: 'So We forgave him that; and indeed, for him is nearness to Us and a good place of return' (38:25). Then: 'O David, indeed We have made you a successor upon the earth, so judge between the people in truth and do not follow [your own] desire' (38:26). The Qur'an does not say what the trial was beyond this, and later stories that fill in details are not from the Qur'an or the Prophet ﷺ, so none are repeated here.

chapters.heading: What the Prophet ﷺ Said of Dawud
chapters.body: The Prophet ﷺ said, as Abu Hurayrah reported: 'The reciting of the Zabur (i.e. Psalms) was made easy for David. He used to order that his riding animals be saddled, and would finish reciting the Zabur before they were saddled. And he would never eat except from the earnings of his manual work' (Sahih al-Bukhari 3417). Abdullah bin Amr reported that the Prophet ﷺ said: 'The most beloved fasting to Allah was the fasting of (the Prophet) David who used to fast on alternate days. And the most beloved prayer to Allah was the prayer of David who used to sleep for (the first) half of the night and pray for 1/3 of it and (again) sleep for a sixth of it' (Sahih al-Bukhari 3420).

familyQuestion: Dawud was a king who still worked with his hands and often turned back to Allah. What work of your own hands can you do for Allah's sake?

title: Adam
subtitle: The first human being, created by Allah, who repented and was forgiven
sources: Qur'an 2:30-39 — the successor on earth, the names, the garden
Qur'an 7:11-27 and 20:115-123 — Iblis, the tree and the forgiveness
Qur'an 15:26-35 and 38:71-76 — the creation from clay
Sahih al-Bukhari 3326 — Adam's greeting; Sahih Muslim 854 — Friday
Sunan Abi Dawud 4693 — the handful of earth (graded Sahih by al-Albani)

chapters.heading: A Successor on Earth
chapters.body: Allah said to the angels: 'Indeed, I will make upon the earth a successive authority.' They asked, 'Will You place upon it one who causes corruption therein and sheds blood, while we declare Your praise and sanctify You?' Allah said, 'Indeed, I know that which you do not know' (2:30). 'He taught Adam the names - all of them' (2:31), and when Adam informed the angels of them, they said, 'Exalted are You; we have no knowledge except what You have taught us' (2:32). The Qur'an says Allah created man 'out of clay' (15:26) and said to the angels: 'when I have proportioned him and breathed into him of My [created] soul, then fall down to him in prostration' (15:29). The Prophet ﷺ said: 'Allah created Adam from a handful which he took from the whole of the earth; so the children of Adam are in accordance with the earth: some red, some white, some black, some a mixture' (Sunan Abi Dawud 4693, graded Sahih by al-Albani). Allah made Adam 60 cubits tall, and Adam greeted the angels with 'As-Salamu Alaikum' (Sahih al-Bukhari 3326).

chapters.heading: Iblis Refuses
chapters.body: 'So the angels prostrated - all of them entirely, Except Iblees; he refused to be with those who prostrated' (15:30-31). Iblis said, 'I am better than him. You created me from fire and created him from clay' (7:12). Allah said, 'Descend from Paradise, for it is not for you to be arrogant therein' (7:13). Iblis asked for a delay until the Day of Resurrection, and said: 'I will surely sit in wait for them on Your straight path' (7:16). Allah told Adam, 'this is an enemy to you and to your wife. Then let him not remove you from Paradise so you would suffer' (20:117).

chapters.heading: The Tree and the Words
chapters.body: 'O Adam, dwell, you and your wife, in Paradise and eat from wherever you will but do not approach this tree, lest you be among the wrongdoers' (7:19). 'Satan whispered to him; he said, «O Adam, shall I direct you to the tree of eternity and possession that will not deteriorate?»' (20:120). He swore to them, 'Indeed, I am to you from among the sincere advisors' (7:21). 'Adam and his wife ate of it' (20:121). The Qur'an says that 'We had already taken a promise from Adam before, but he forgot; and We found not in him determination' (20:115). Then they said: 'Our Lord, we have wronged ourselves, and if You do not forgive us and have mercy upon us, we will surely be among the losers' (7:23). 'Then Adam received from his Lord [some] words, and He accepted his repentance. Indeed, it is He who is the Accepting of repentance, the Merciful' (2:37). 'Then his Lord chose him and turned to him in forgiveness and guided [him]' (20:122).

chapters.heading: The Descent and the Guidance
chapters.body: 'Descend, being to one another enemies. And for you on the earth is a place of settlement and enjoyment for a time' (7:24). Allah said: 'when guidance comes to you from Me, whoever follows My guidance - there will be no fear concerning them, nor will they grieve' (2:38). The Qur'an warns the children of Adam: 'let not Satan tempt you as he removed your parents from Paradise' (7:27), and says 'the clothing of righteousness - that is best' (7:26). The Prophet ﷺ said: 'The best day on which the sun has risen is Friday; on it Adam was created, on it he was made to enter Paradise, on it he was expelled from it' (Sahih Muslim 854).

familyQuestion: Adam made a mistake, then asked for forgiveness and was forgiven. What does his story tell you to do when you make one?

title: Ishaq (Isaac)
subtitle: The learned son promised to Ibrahim, a prophet among the righteous
sources: Qur'an 11:69-73, 15:51-56, 51:24-30 — the glad tidings
Qur'an 38:45-47 and 29:27 — chosen for remembrance of the Hereafter
Qur'an 2:132-133 and 4:163 — the faith of the fathers
Sahih al-Bukhari 3390 — the Prophet ﷺ on the line of Yusuf

chapters.heading: The Glad Tidings
chapters.body: The angels came to Ibrahim عليه السلام with good tidings; they said, 'Peace.' He said, 'Peace,' and did not delay in bringing [them] a roasted calf (11:69). When he saw their hands not reaching for it, they said, 'Fear not. We have been sent to the people of Lot' (11:70). 'His wife was standing, and she smiled. Then We gave her good tidings of Isaac and after Isaac, Jacob' (11:71). She said, 'Woe to me! Shall I give birth while I am an old woman and this, my husband, is an old man? Indeed, this is an amazing thing!' (11:72). They said, 'Are you amazed at the decree of Allah?' (11:73). To Ibrahim they said: 'we give you good tidings of a learned boy' (15:53). When he said 'Have you given me good tidings although old age has come upon me?', they answered, 'We have given you good tidings in truth, so do not be of the despairing' (15:54-55). He said, 'And who despairs of the mercy of his Lord except for those astray?' (15:56).

chapters.heading: A Prophet and a Leader
chapters.body: Allah says: 'We gave him Isaac and Jacob, and each [of them] We made a prophet. And We gave them of Our mercy, and we made for them a reputation of high honor' (19:49-50). He also says: 'We made them leaders guiding by Our command. And We inspired to them the doing of good deeds, establishment of prayer, and giving of zakah; and they were worshippers of Us' (21:73). 'And We gave him good tidings of Isaac, a prophet from among the righteous' (37:112). Ishaq is listed among those to whom revelation came (4:163), and among those whom Allah describes: 'those of strength and [religious] vision. Indeed, We chose them for an exclusive quality: remembrance of the home [of the Hereafter]' (38:45-46). When Ya'qub was dying, his sons said: 'We will worship your God and the God of your fathers, Abraham and Ishmael and Isaac - one God' (2:133).

chapters.heading: The Line of Prophets
chapters.body: The Prophet ﷺ said, as Ibn Umar reported: 'The honorable, the son of the honorable, the son of the honorable, the son of the honorable, (was) Joseph, the son of Jacob, the son of Isaac, the son of Abraham' (Sahih al-Bukhari 3390). The Qur'an says Allah placed 'in his descendants prophethood and scripture' (29:27). Outside this the Qur'an gives no further story of Ishaq's own life, so none is added here.

familyQuestion: Ibrahim said, 'Who despairs of the mercy of his Lord except for those astray?' When has hope in Allah's mercy helped you?

title: Ya'qub (Jacob)
subtitle: The father of Yusuf, a prophet of beautiful patience
sources: Qur'an 12:4-18, 12:64-68 and 12:83-100 — Ya'qub in Surah Yusuf
Qur'an 19:49-50, 21:72-73, 38:45-47 — a prophet and a leader
Qur'an 2:132-133 — his advice to his sons
Sahih al-Bukhari 3390 — the Prophet ﷺ on the line of Yusuf

chapters.heading: The Dream and the Warning
chapters.body: Yusuf told his father, 'O my father, indeed I have seen [in a dream] eleven stars and the sun and the moon; I saw them prostrating to me' (12:4). Ya'qub عليه السلام said: 'O my son, do not relate your vision to your brothers or they will contrive against you a plan. Indeed Satan, to man, is a manifest enemy. And thus will your Lord choose you and teach you the interpretation of narratives and complete His favor upon you and upon the family of Jacob, as He completed it upon your fathers before, Abraham and Isaac' (12:5-6). Later the brothers asked him to send Yusuf with them. He said, 'it saddens me that you should take him, and I fear that a wolf would eat him while you are of him unaware' (12:13).

chapters.heading: The Shirt
chapters.body: The brothers came at night, weeping, and said, 'a wolf ate him. But you would not believe us, even if we were truthful' (12:17). 'And they brought upon his shirt false blood. [Jacob] said, «Rather, your souls have enticed you to something, so patience is most fitting. And Allah is the one sought for help against that which you describe»' (12:18). Years later, after another of his sons was kept in Egypt (12:79-80), he said again: 'Rather, your souls have enticed you to something, so patience is most fitting. Perhaps Allah will bring them to me all together' (12:83). 'And he turned away from them and said, «Oh, my sorrow over Joseph,» and his eyes became white from grief, for he was [of that] a suppressor' (12:84).

chapters.heading: Hope and Reunion
chapters.body: He said: 'I only complain of my suffering and my grief to Allah, and I know from Allah that which you do not know. O my sons, go and find out about Joseph and his brother and despair not of relief from Allah. Indeed, no one despairs of relief from Allah except the disbelieving people' (12:86-87). When the caravan left Egypt, he said, 'Indeed, I find the smell of Joseph [and would say that he was alive] if you did not think me weakened in mind' (12:94). The shirt was cast over his face and 'he returned [once again] seeing. He said, «Did I not tell you that I know from Allah that which you do not know?»' (12:96). When his sons asked him to seek forgiveness for them, he said, 'I will ask forgiveness for you from my Lord. Indeed, it is He who is the Forgiving, the Merciful' (12:98). In Egypt Yusuf said, 'O my father, this is the explanation of my vision of before. My Lord has made it reality' (12:100).

chapters.heading: His Last Advice
chapters.body: Allah says of Ya'qub's advice: 'Abraham instructed his sons [to do the same] and [so did] Jacob, [saying], «O my sons, indeed Allah has chosen for you this religion, so do not die except while you are Muslims»' (2:132). 'When death approached Jacob, ... he said to his sons, «What will you worship after me?»' They said, 'We will worship your God and the God of your fathers, Abraham and Ishmael and Isaac - one God. And we are Muslims [in submission] to Him' (2:133). The Qur'an counts him among the prophets: 'We gave him Isaac and Jacob, and each [of them] We made a prophet' (19:49).

familyQuestion: Ya'qub said, 'patience is most fitting,' and kept hoping for years. What is something you can keep hoping for with patience?

title: Shu'ayb
subtitle: The prophet sent to Madyan who called for honest weights and measures
sources: Qur'an 7:85-93 — fulfil the measure and weight
Qur'an 11:84-95 — his words and the end of Madyan
Qur'an 26:176-191 — the companions of the thicket
Qur'an 15:78-79 — the thicket and the clear highway

chapters.heading: Full Measure and Weight
chapters.body: Allah says: 'And to [the people of] Madyan [We sent] their brother Shu'ayb. He said, «O my people, worship Allah; you have no deity other than Him. There has come to you clear evidence from your Lord. So fulfill the measure and weight and do not deprive people of their due and cause not corruption upon the earth after its reformation. That is better for you, if you should be believers»' (7:85). In another place: 'And O my people, give full measure and weight in justice and do not deprive the people of their due and do not commit abuse on the earth, spreading corruption. What remains [lawful] from Allah is best for you, if you would be believers. But I am not a guardian over you' (11:85-86). To the companions of the thicket he said: 'Give full measure and do not be of those who cause loss. And weigh with an even balance' (26:181-182). Shu'ayb عليه السلام also said, 'do not sit on every path, threatening and averting from the way of Allah those who believe in Him' (7:86).

chapters.heading: Their Answer
chapters.body: They said, 'O Shu'ayb, does your prayer command you that we should leave what our fathers worship or not do with our wealth what we please?' (11:87). He answered, 'I do not intend to differ from you in that which I have forbidden you; I only intend reform as much as I am able. And my success is not but through Allah. Upon Him I have relied, and to Him I return' (11:88). They said, 'we consider you among us as weak. And if not for your family, we would have stoned you [to death]' (11:91). The arrogant ones threatened: 'We will surely evict you, O Shu'ayb, and those who have believed with you from our city, or you must return to our religion.' He said, 'Even if we were unwilling?' (7:88). The believers said, 'Upon Allah we have relied. Our Lord, decide between us and our people in truth, and You are the best of those who give decision' (7:89).

chapters.heading: The End
chapters.body: 'And when Our command came, We saved Shu'ayb and those who believed with him, by mercy from Us. And the shriek seized those who had wronged, and they became within their homes [corpses] fallen prone' (11:94). Of the companions of the thicket the Qur'an says: 'the punishment of the day of the black cloud seized them. Indeed, it was the punishment of a terrible day' (26:189). Shu'ayb 'turned away from them and said, «O my people, I had certainly conveyed to you the messages of my Lord and advised you, so how could I grieve for a disbelieving people?»' (7:93). The Qur'an names both Madyan and the companions of the thicket, each with their own verses, and this story does not decide how the two are related.

familyQuestion: Shu'ayb taught that cheating in trade is a sin against Allah. Where in your own buying and selling do you need to weigh with an even balance?

title: Ayyub (Job)
subtitle: The patient servant who called on the Most Merciful
sources: Qur'an 21:83-84 — 'adversity has touched me'
Qur'an 38:41-44 — the spring and the bunch of grass
Qur'an 4:163 and 6:84 — counted among the prophets
Sahih al-Bukhari 3391 — the Prophet ﷺ on Ayyub and the gold locusts

chapters.heading: The Call
chapters.body: 'And [mention] Job, when he called to his Lord, «Indeed, adversity has touched me, and you are the Most Merciful of the merciful»' (21:83). In Surah Sad: 'when he called to his Lord, «Indeed, Satan has touched me with hardship and torment»' (38:41). The Qur'an does not describe his illness or his losses in detail, so this story does not add any. Allah lists him among the prophets: 'David and Solomon and Job and Joseph and Moses and Aaron. Thus do We reward the doers of good' (6:84). He is also named among those to whom revelation came (4:163).

chapters.heading: The Answer
chapters.body: Allah said: 'Strike [the ground] with your foot; this is a [spring for] a cool bath and drink' (38:42). 'So We responded to him and removed what afflicted him of adversity. And We gave him [back] his family and the like thereof with them as mercy from Us and a reminder for the worshippers [of Allah]' (21:84). Allah also told him: 'take in your hand a bunch [of grass] and strike with it and do not break your oath' (38:44). Then: 'Indeed, We found him patient, an excellent servant. Indeed, he was one repeatedly turning back [to Allah]' (38:44). The Qur'an does not say what the oath was.

chapters.heading: The Gold Locusts
chapters.body: The Prophet ﷺ said, as Abu Hurayrah reported: 'While Job was naked, taking a bath, a swarm of gold locusts fell on him and he started collecting them in his garment. His Lord called him, «O Job! Have I not made you rich enough to need what you see?» He said, «Yes, O Lord! But I cannot dispense with your Blessing»' (Sahih al-Bukhari 3391).

familyQuestion: Ayyub said only, 'You are the Most Merciful of the merciful.' What would be your own short call to Allah on your hardest day?

title: Sulayman (Solomon)
subtitle: The king who inherited from Dawud, thankful for what Allah gave him
sources: Qur'an 38:30-40 — 'a kingdom such as will not belong to anyone after me'
Qur'an 27:15-44 — the ant, the hoopoe and the Queen of Sheba
Qur'an 34:12-14 and 21:78-82 — the wind, the jinn, the judgement
Qur'an 2:102 — it was not Solomon who disbelieved
Sahih al-Bukhari 3427 — the Prophet ﷺ on the judgement of Sulayman

chapters.heading: A Kingdom Given and Asked
chapters.body: 'And to David We gave Solomon. An excellent servant, indeed he was one repeatedly turning back [to Allah]' (38:30). Solomon said: 'My Lord, forgive me and grant me a kingdom such as will not belong to anyone after me. Indeed, You are the Bestower' (38:35). 'So We subjected to him the wind blowing by his command, gently, wherever he directed, And [also] the devils [of jinn] - every builder and diver' (38:36-37). 'This is Our gift, so grant or withhold without account' (38:39). 'And indeed, for him is nearness to Us and a good place of return' (38:40). 'Solomon inherited David. He said, «O people, we have been taught the language of birds, and we have been given from all things. Indeed, this is evident bounty»' (27:16).

chapters.heading: The Ant and the Hoopoe
chapters.body: Solomon's armies of 'jinn and men and birds' marched (27:17). 'Until, when they came upon the valley of the ants, an ant said, «O ants, enter your dwellings that you not be crushed by Solomon and his soldiers while they perceive not.» So [Solomon] smiled, amused at her speech, and said, «My Lord, enable me to be grateful for Your favor which You have bestowed upon me and upon my parents and to do righteousness of which You approve»' (27:18-19). He noticed the hoopoe was missing. The hoopoe returned and said, 'I have encompassed [in knowledge] that which you have not encompassed, and I have come to you from Sheba with certain news. Indeed, I found [there] a woman ruling them' (27:22-23), who with her people prostrated to the sun instead of Allah (27:24). Solomon said, 'We will see whether you were truthful or were of the liars' (27:27).

chapters.heading: The Letter and the Throne
chapters.body: He sent a letter: 'In the name of Allah, the Entirely Merciful, the Especially Merciful, Be not haughty with me but come to me in submission [as Muslims]' (27:30-31). The queen consulted her chiefs and sent a gift. Solomon said, 'what Allah has given me is better than what He has given you' (27:36). When he saw her throne placed before him, he said, 'This is from the favor of my Lord to test me whether I will be grateful or ungrateful. And whoever is grateful - his gratitude is only for [the benefit of] himself' (27:40). When she entered the palace and thought its floor was water, he said it was 'made smooth with glass.' She said, 'My Lord, indeed I have wronged myself, and I submit with Solomon to Allah, Lord of the worlds' (27:44).

chapters.heading: Judgement and Gratitude
chapters.body: Of the case of the field, Allah says: 'We gave understanding of the case to Solomon, and to each [of them] We gave judgement and knowledge' (21:79). Allah said to the family of David: 'Work, O family of David, in gratitude. And few of My servants are grateful' (34:13). About his death: 'nothing indicated to the jinn his death except a creature of the earth eating his staff' (34:14). The Qur'an also clears him of the lies about magic: 'It was not Solomon who disbelieved, but the devils disbelieved' (2:102). The Prophet ﷺ told of two women who disputed over a child, and Solomon son of David said, 'Bring me a knife so as to cut the child into two pieces and distribute it between them.' The younger woman said, 'May Allah be merciful to you! Don't do that, for it is her child,' and he gave the child to her (Sahih al-Bukhari 3427).

familyQuestion: Sulayman had everything and still asked to be grateful. What have you not thanked Allah for this week?

title: Dhul-Kifl
subtitle: Named in the Qur'an among the patient and the outstanding
sources: Qur'an 21:85-86 — among the patient, admitted into mercy
Qur'an 38:48 — among the outstanding

chapters.heading: What the Qur'an Says
chapters.body: Dhul-Kifl عليه السلام is named twice in the Qur'an. Allah says: 'And [mention] Ishmael and Idrees and Dhul-Kifl; all were of the patient. And We admitted them into Our mercy. Indeed, they were of the righteous' (21:85-86). And: 'And remember Ishmael, Elisha and Dhul-Kifl, and all are among the outstanding' (38:48). The Qur'an gives no story about him. This story adds none, and scholars differ about who he was, so no identification is given here.

chapters.heading: Why the Few Words Matter
chapters.body: In these verses Allah gives him three descriptions: patient, admitted into His mercy, and among the outstanding. In the same verses are other prophets, Ismail, Idris and Al-Yasa. Whatever else is not known, a person can be remembered by Allah for patience and righteousness without a long biography.

familyQuestion: Allah describes Dhul-Kifl as patient and outstanding without telling his story. Which of your quiet qualities do you hope Allah values?

title: Harun (Aaron)
subtitle: Musa's brother and helper, given as a prophet by Allah's mercy
sources: Qur'an 20:25-36 — Musa's request for Harun
Qur'an 19:51-53 and 25:35 — a prophet by Allah's mercy
Qur'an 7:142 and 20:83-94 — left in charge, and the calf
Qur'an 7:148-155 — Harun's words to Musa
Sahih Muslim 2135 — 'sister of Harun'

chapters.heading: The Answer to Musa's Prayer
chapters.body: Musa عليه السلام prayed: 'My Lord, expand for me my breast [with assurance] And ease for me my task And untie the knot from my tongue That they may understand my speech. And appoint for me a minister from my family - Aaron, my brother. Increase through him my strength And let him share my task' (20:25-32). Allah said: 'You have been granted your request, O Moses' (20:36). And: 'We gave him out of Our mercy his brother Aaron as a prophet' (19:53). 'We had certainly given Moses the Scripture and appointed with him his brother Aaron as an assistant' (25:35). The two were sent together 'with Our signs and a clear authority' (23:45).

chapters.heading: Left in Charge
chapters.body: When Musa went for the appointment, he said to Harun: 'Take my place among my people, do right [by them], and do not follow the way of the corrupters' (7:142). While Musa was away, the Samiri made a calf, and the people said, 'This is your god and the god of Moses' (20:88). Harun had already told them: 'O my people, you are only being tested by it, and indeed, your Lord is the Most Merciful, so follow me and obey my order.' They said, 'We will never cease being devoted to the calf until Moses returns to us' (20:90-91).

chapters.heading: Harun and Musa
chapters.body: Musa returned angry and grieved and asked Harun, 'what prevented you, when you saw them going astray, From following me?' (20:92-93). Harun said: 'O son of my mother, do not seize [me] by my beard or by my head. Indeed, I feared that you would say, «You caused division among the Children of Israel, and you did not observe [or await] my word»' (20:94). In Surah al-A'raf he said, 'the people oppressed me and were about to kill me, so let not the enemies rejoice over me' (7:150). Musa said: 'My Lord, forgive me and my brother and admit us into Your mercy, for You are the most merciful of the merciful' (7:151). The Qur'an also calls Maryam 'sister of Aaron' (19:28). The Prophet ﷺ explained, as Mughira bin Shu'ba reported, that people of old gave names after prophets and pious persons who had gone before them (Sahih Muslim 2135).

familyQuestion: Musa asked Allah for a helper and was given his brother. Who helps you carry your tasks, and have you thanked them?

title: Ilyas (Elijah)
subtitle: The messenger who asked his people to leave Ba'l and fear Allah
sources: Qur'an 37:123-132 — Elias among the messengers
Qur'an 6:85 — among the righteous

chapters.heading: The Call
chapters.body: 'And indeed, Elias was from among the messengers, When he said to his people, «Will you not fear Allah? Do you call upon Ba'l and leave the best of creators - Allah, your Lord and the Lord of your first forefathers?»' (37:123-126). The Qur'an adds: 'And they denied him, so indeed, they will be brought [for punishment], Except the chosen servants of Allah' (37:127-128).

chapters.heading: Peace upon Ilyas
chapters.body: Allah says: 'And We left for him [favorable mention] among later generations: «Peace upon Elias.» Indeed, We thus reward the doers of good. Indeed, he was of Our believing servants' (37:129-132). He is also counted among the righteous: 'And Zechariah and John and Jesus and Elias - and all were of the righteous' (6:85). The Qur'an gives no further events from his life, so this story does not add any.

familyQuestion: Ilyas asked his people why they followed Ba'l. Is there something you follow only because others always have?

title: Al-Yasa (Elisha)
subtitle: Preferred over the worlds and counted among the outstanding
sources: Qur'an 6:86 — preferred over the worlds
Qur'an 38:48 — among the outstanding

chapters.heading: What the Qur'an Says
chapters.body: Al-Yasa عليه السلام is named twice in the Qur'an. Allah says: 'And Ishmael and Elisha and Jonah and Lot - and all [of them] We preferred over the worlds' (6:86). And: 'And remember Ishmael, Elisha and Dhul-Kifl, and all are among the outstanding' (38:48). The Qur'an gives no event from his life. This story does not add any.

chapters.heading: A Place Among the Prophets
chapters.body: He is named with Ismail, Yunus, Lut and Dhul-Kifl. Allah calls them 'preferred over the worlds' (6:86) and 'outstanding' (38:48). For a believer, that is the full picture the Qur'an gives: chosen by Allah and remembered with honour.

familyQuestion: Allah honoured Al-Yasa with only two verses. What matters more to you: being known by people, or being known to Allah?

title: The River Kept Him
subtitle: A mother trusted Allah's inspiration and her son was returned to her
sources: Qur'an 28:7-13 — the inspiration, the river and the return
Qur'an 20:37-40 — Allah's favour upon Musa

chapters.heading: The Inspiration
chapters.body: Allah says: 'And We inspired to the mother of Moses, «Suckle him; but when you fear for him, cast him into the river and do not fear and do not grieve. Indeed, We will return him to you and will make him [one] of the messengers»' (28:7). In Surah Ta-Ha, Allah reminds Musa: 'Cast him into the chest and cast it into the river, and the river will throw it onto the bank; there will take him an enemy to Me and an enemy to him.
